body.zh-HK:
> 面試官問：「model 冇換，但 p99 latency 突然升高。你會由邊度開始搵？」
>
> 答啱一半嘅答案：「我會加更多 GPU。」

GPU 有可能係答案，但 p99 先係一個症狀。第 99 個最慢 request 可能根本未到 model：它可能等緊 batch、重試一個慢 tool、被一個很長 input 佔住 prefill，或者先在 network timeout 裡兜了一圈。只睇平均值或 GPU utilisation，會把不同的慢混成同一個容量問題。

## P99 的慢，藏在哪一段

替每個 request 留一個 trace ID，把路徑切成 arrival、queue、retrieval／tool、prefill、decode、output validation、retry 和 response stream。每段同時記錄版本、route、input／output token bucket、cache state 和最後 result。然後只抽 p99 的 request 看：它們是否集中在同一個 deployment、同一類長 input、同一個 external dependency，還是只在 traffic burst 時出現？沒有這條時間線，『加 GPU』只是昂貴的猜測。

## 把長尾分成可處理的類別

Queue time 高而 decode 正常，先看 admission、concurrency limit、batch policy 或一群 request 同時 retry；prefill 高而 input length 飆升，先查 context 組裝和 retrieval；tool time 高，GPU 不會救到對方 service 的 timeout。若 decode time 和 GPU util 同時長期偏高，而且其他段穩定，才有較強理由試較多或較合適的 compute。每個假設都要有一個預期：改動後哪一段會下降，哪一段不應惡化。

## 用負載測試重現尾巴

本地 demo 不要只送一條短 prompt 一百次。做一組 synthetic fixtures：短和長 input、cache hit/miss、需要 tool 的 request、被拒絕的 input 和一次可控 dependency slowdown。以幾個固定 concurrency level 跑 baseline 和 candidate，報 p50、p95、p99、timeout、retry count、queue age 和 cost proxy。把成功率與 p99 放在一起看；把 request 快速超時不算成性能進步。

## 你如何把答案講成決定

可以說：『我會先定位 p99 究竟花在 queue、input、model 還是 dependency，再做一個只改該段的受控實驗。若 GPU 增加後 p99 沒改善，我會保留 baseline，而不是把它包裝成 scale-up。』這句話表明你知道 tail latency 是 user 等候、服務成本和可靠性共同的問題。

## 交畀 reviewer 的檢查點

- **工程：** trace schema、stage-duration chart、token／route slice、synthetic load harness 和一個重現 tail 的 fixture。
- **交付：** 哪一種 request 可以降級成較快的安全回覆、何時顯示稍後重試、以及誰負責 external dependency。
- **取捨：** batch 可能提升吞吐卻拉長個別等待；縮短 output 可能改善 decode 卻少了必要 caveat。兩個都要量度，不要只報一個平均數。

## 延伸閱讀

[平均快咗，P99 可以更差](/zh-HK/interview-lab/a-faster-average-can-hide-a-worse-p99)、[Queue 要有 dead-letter path](/zh-HK/interview-lab/a-queue-needs-a-dead-letter-path) 和 [Model routing 要有 fallback](/zh-HK/interview-lab/model-routing-needs-a-fallback)。

body.en:
> Interviewer asks: “The model has not changed, but p99 latency suddenly climbed. Where do you begin?”
>
> Half-right answer: “I would add more GPUs.”

A GPU may eventually be part of the answer, but p99 is a symptom first. The slowest one per cent of requests may never have reached the model: they may be waiting for a batch, retrying a slow tool, spending prefill on a large input, or taking a lap through a network timeout. An average or a GPU-utilisation chart merges those different kinds of slow into one capacity story.

## Find the stage hiding the tail

Give every request a trace ID and divide its path into arrival, queue, retrieval or tool, prefill, decode, output validation, retry, and response streaming. Record version, route, input/output token bucket, cache state and final result at each stage. Then inspect only p99 requests: do they cluster around one deployment, one long-input class, one external dependency, or a traffic burst? Without that timeline, adding GPUs is an expensive guess.

## Turn the tail into treatable categories

High queue time with normal decode points to admission, a concurrency limit, batching policy, or a retry storm. High prefill alongside longer inputs points to context assembly or retrieval. High tool time is not repaired by a GPU. If decode time and GPU utilisation are persistently high while other stages remain stable, there is a stronger case for more or different compute. Every hypothesis needs an expectation: which stage should fall after the change, and which must not get worse.

## Reproduce the tail under load

A local demo should not send one short prompt one hundred times. Build synthetic fixtures for short and long inputs, cache hit/miss, tool-using requests, rejected inputs, and one controlled dependency slowdown. At fixed concurrency levels, compare baseline and candidate on p50, p95, p99, timeout rate, retries, queue age and a cost proxy. Read success rate next to p99; a request that fails quickly is not a performance win.

## State the answer as a decision

You can say: ‘I would first locate whether p99 is spent in the queue, input, model or dependency, then run a controlled experiment that changes that stage only. If additional GPUs do not improve p99, I keep the baseline rather than calling it a scale-up.’ That connects tail latency to user waiting, service cost and reliability.

## Checkpoints a reviewer can inspect

- **Engineering:** a trace schema, stage-duration chart, token/route slices, synthetic load harness, and a fixture that recreates a tail.
- **Delivery:** which request can degrade to a faster safe response, when users see retry-later, and who owns an external dependency.
- **Trade-off:** batching can improve throughput while extending individual waits; shorter output can improve decode while omitting a necessary caveat. Measure both instead of reporting one average.

## Further reading

[A faster average can hide a worse P99](/en/interview-lab/a-faster-average-can-hide-a-worse-p99), [A queue needs a dead-letter path](/en/interview-lab/a-queue-needs-a-dead-letter-path), and [Model routing needs a fallback](/en/interview-lab/model-routing-needs-a-fallback).

## Scope note

This is an AI.DOG single-question practice exercise. Traces, traffic, dependencies and metrics are synthetic teaching material, not observations from a service or a capacity recommendation.
